sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head dark brown, broadly oval, covered with hairs of moderate length; fontanelle about as large as the ocelli, white and conspicuous; two large muscle attachment scars in front of the ocelli; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 small, segment 4 shorter than segment 2; compound eyes of moderate size, not very close to the lower margin of the head; ocelli rather large, separated from the compound eyes by less than their width; postclypeus paler than the head, without a median line; pronotum paler than the head, its posterior margin and sides forming a nearly even arc, anterior angles pointed, a pale line in the middle; posterior margin of meso- and metanotum narrow and deeply concave; wings smoky, veins throughout fairly distinct.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, broadly oval, covered with hairs of moderate length. Two large muscle attachment scars in front of the ocelli. Fontanelle about as large as the ocelli, white and conspicuous. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 small, segment 4 shorter than segment 2. Compound eyes of moderate size, not very close to the lower margin of the head; ocelli rather large, separated from the compound eyes by less than their width. Postclypeus paler than the head, without a visible median line. Pronotum paler than the head, posterior margin and sides forming a nearly even arc, anterior angles pointed; a pale line in the middle of the pronotum. Posterior margin of meso- and metanotum narrow and deeply concave. Wings smoky, veins throughout fairly distinct. Abdominal tergites concolorous with the pronotum, each with a pale spot on the anterior margin. Measurements: alate body length 9.50—10.50 mm, dealate body length 4.50—6.20 mm; head length 0.97 mm, head width 0.83—0.87 mm; antenna length 1.43—1.50 mm; eye diameter 0.23 mm; pronotum length 0.41—0.46 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality Kartabo, British Guiana. Holotype an alate. The description is based on numerous alates and dealate reproductives collected by the author in eleven different nests at Kartabo.
